newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bank Qld no comment on St George bid talk.
newsitem.headline: Bank Qld no comment on St George bid talk.

text.p: Bank of Queensland Ltd said on Monday it had no comment on media speculation that St George Bank Ltd was interested in acquiring control.
But the Queensland regional bank said it expected talks with the Queensland state government, owner of a 44.5 percent stake in the Bank of Queensland, would eventuate in due course.
"We don't make comment on unsourced speculation and a rumour," Bank of Queensland chairman Neil Roberts told Reuters.
Roberts was referring to a report in the Sydney Morning Herald on Monday that said St George had expressed an interest in acquiring control of the Queensland bank.

The state government's holding in bank of Queensland was housed in its Queenland Treasury Corporation (QTC) late last year after Bank of Queensland declined an offer to join in the merger of the Suncorp finance giant Queensland Industry Development Corp (QIDC) and Metway Bank Ltd MWB.AX.
Following directions from the Australian Treasury the state government is required to sell down its Bank of Queensland sake to under 10 percent within three years.
"I have every expectation there will be discussions with the state government in due course as to the ultimate destination of the shares to be sold," Roberts said.
"Meanwhile, we are getting on with the business of the bank," Roberts said.
St George Bank officials were unavailable for comment.
Bank of Queensland shares were three cents higher at A$5.18 at 12.45 p.m. (0245 GMT) on Monday, while St George Bank shares were 19 cents stronger at A$8.72.
